name: Lamu
tagline: Swahili stone town of donkeys and dhows
summary: Lamu Old Town is the oldest continuously lived-in Swahili town in East Africa, a car-free UNESCO maze of coral-stone houses, carved doors and donkeys. Sail at sunset on a dhow, walk the beach to Shela, see the Lamu Fort and museum, and let the island's slow pace take over.
seasonNote: Avoid the long rains of April to June; check current travel advice for the Lamu area before you go.
arrival: Flights from Nairobi and Mombasa land on Manda Island, then a short boat ride.
gettingAround: Walk, donkey or boat; there are almost no cars.
cashTip: Carry shillings; M-Pesa is used everywhere but needs a local SIM. Tip about 10 percent.
foodTip: Swahili seafood curries, coconut rice, samaki wa kupaka and fresh juices.
buyTip: Carved Lamu doors and furniture, and dhow models.
baseArea: Lamu Old Town or Shela village
